answer: Verifiable delay gating: every epoch each identity must publish a VDF output over (id, epoch), accepted only in a short window. A VDF is serial, so one machine cannot mint two identities in time; an attacker running an orchard of clones must buy one core per fake identity, every epoch. The cost is mirrored in hardware, not fees. Clones on one host betray themselves via a spiral of round-trip delays as load pushes proofs outside the window; packed tighter, the spiral closes and the cluster is pruned. Per-clone cost is silicon and electricity, paid forever.
